terms.def: A KMSC staff member at a site, responsible for a set of phones, one operator for every ten phones. The operator hands out the phones, restarts them, and manages the wearers.
The person who wears the phone and records the video, either a site employee or a worker we recruited. Every wearer passes onboarding screening.
The set of sites that one Portfolio Manager owns. Each portfolio has a monthly hour target.
The setup day at a new site, before official filming starts. We set up the stations, labels, and network, give the orientation, and make the pilot recordings.
One recording period of 30 minutes. The collection app stops at 30 minutes, then the phone is restarted and the next cycle starts.
The online form the site lead submits by 6:00 PM, one per site, direct and partner. It goes into the company database, and the company report builds itself from it.
The page that adds up every site's daily report. At 6:15 PM the chase list of missing sites goes to Mano. At 8:00 PM the number posts on its own.

The senior operator on a floor with 20 or more phones. Reports to the Portfolio Manager. Does the 7 AM count with the Portfolio Manager, runs the floor between visits, and submits the daily report by 6:00 PM. A partner site has one too.
A review note on one video, either feedback or fraud. Feedback means something to fix, and fraud means the video is not paid, a penalty, and a possible ban.
A warning on an account. Two strikes pause the phone until the worker is retrained.
The unique ID of one recorded video in the export. QC uses it to link a flag to one video.
The record that shows who wore which phone on which shift.
Footage recorded but not uploaded yet, measured in device-days. More than one day at a site is an incident.
A place with a fast internet line. We bring the phones to the hub, and they upload overnight. There are two: Central and East.
The checklist that every wearer completes before a phone goes on their head.
The daily meeting of Adham, Moharam, and Mano.
Thirty minutes every day when any operator can talk directly to leadership.
A performance improvement plan that lasts 7 days. It comes with a written warning.
If you bring us a site contract, you get 10% on that contract. If you refer a person and we hire them, you get 2,000 EGP.
Any place where people expect more privacy than usual. We never film there.

ownership: Mano owns this map and approves every change. Every edit gets one changelog line with a version and a date.

changelog.text: A Planning and Logistics Lead under Moharam owns the dispatch schedule, the store, the two hubs, the runners, the lines, and the gear. Mano keeps recruiting, papers, wearer files, and this map. A site lead on every floor with 20 or more phones. The daily report is an online form, sent by the site lead by 6:00 PM, and the company report builds itself. Two hubs, Central and East. No HR seat and no business development seat. Month end pays on our own audit, then invoices the client.

Jobs: one page per role with the handbook, the posting for job boards, and the offer letter. Uploading rewritten around two ways to upload and three hubs. The company name is gone from every page. Procedures are grouped by role. The capacity calculator splits direct operations from delivery partners. The legal calendar is gone. Every page was cut shorter and simpler, in English and Arabic. Print buttons work inside the preview.

Rebuilt the map as a site, with every section on its own page and the content in JSON files. Added channels, incident playbooks, training, metrics, risks, the never list, the letter generator, the capacity calculator, six more manual subsystems, Arabic for the pages workers use, and print styles.

The whole map on one page: the people, who to call, the nine-stage workflow, the working day, the rules, onboarding screening, the glossary, and the first two manual subsystems, data logistics and asset control.
